source: The Local Approved Ten-Day Tokyo Itinerary (Neighborhood Guide), bought for the family. 28 neighbourhoods, 10 flexible one-day walks. Spot tuples are [name, category, note?, mapsQuery?].

nakameguro.name: Nakameguro
nakameguro.vibe: Cafés over the tracks and small shops along the Meguro river.

daikanyama.name: Daikanyama
daikanyama.vibe: Design shops, the Tsutaya bookshop and a Taisho-era house.

ebisu.name: Ebisu
ebisu.vibe: Offices by day, izakayas and cocktail bars by night.

tomigaya.name: Tomigaya
tomigaya.vibe: Shibuya's quiet pocket, full of bakeries and cafés.

harajuku.name: Harajuku
harajuku.vibe: The Meiji shrine, Cat Street and the backstreets.

shibuya.name: Shibuya
shibuya.vibe: The crossing, the observation decks and the Hikarie food hall.

asakusa.name: Asakusa
asakusa.vibe: Tokyo's oldest temple, with the Skytree across the river.

yanaka.name: Yanaka
yanaka.vibe: Red torii, quiet residential streets and the Yanaka Ginza.

ueno.name: Ueno Park
ueno.vibe: The big museums and the Shinobazu pond.

kiyosumi.name: Kiyosumi
kiyosumi.vibe: Tokyo's coffee district and a preserved garden.

ningyocho.name: Ningyocho
ningyocho.vibe: Century-old sweet shops and old Tokyo.

ginza.name: Ginza
ginza.vibe: Eight-floor stationers, kissaten and creative conveyor-belt sushi.

shinjuku.name: Shinjuku
shinjuku.vibe: The Gyoen park, old kissaten and department stores.

hatagaya.name: Hatagaya
hatagaya.vibe: Three overlooked neighbourhoods of thoughtful cafés and shops.

shimokitazawa.name: Shimokitazawa
shimokitazawa.vibe: Vintage shops, independent cafés and creative energy.

kichijoji.name: Kichijōji
kichijoji.vibe: The Inokashira pond and an underground café from another decade.

nakano.name: Nakano
nakano.vibe: Nakano Broadway and lantern-lined alleys of izakayas.

jiyugaoka.name: Jiyugaoka
jiyugaoka.vibe: Tree-lined streets with a European air on the Toyoko line.

gakugeidai.name: Gakugei-dai
gakugeidai.vibe: Everyday Tokyo: greengrocers, students and bookshops.

yutenji.name: Yutenji
yutenji.vibe: A quiet residential stretch between Gakugei-dai and Nakameguro.

aoyama.name: Aoyama
aoyama.vibe: Refined architecture, bakeries and the Nezu Museum garden.

roppongi.name: Roppongi
roppongi.vibe: Contemporary art, special dinners and jazz.

kuramae.name: Kuramae
kuramae.vibe: The makers' neighbourhood: stationery, baskets and leather.

jimbocho.name: Jimbocho
jimbocho.vibe: Secondhand bookshops, curry and classic kissaten.

akihabara.name: Akihabara
akihabara.vibe: Neon, the Mansei bridge and shops from another world.

tsukiji.name: Tsukiji
tsukiji.vibe: The fish market, with the Hamarikyu garden next door.

imperial.name: Imperial Palace
imperial.vibe: Wide paths, gardens and the modern art museum.

kagurazaka.name: Kagurazaka
kagurazaka.vibe: Narrow backstreets, bistros and a French note in old Tokyo.

routes.tagline: Sipping at cafés, local bakeries, nature walks, a traditional home, bookshops and lively izakayas
routes.reflect: Was there a dish or flavour from today that you'd like to try recreating, or learn more about?

moves.title: Travel to Nakameguro and enjoy the local cafés
moves.text: Nakameguro Station is where you discover local life and plenty of neighbourhood cafés. Enjoy a latte and watch the trains go by upstairs at Onibus. Along the river, visit Sidewalk Stand for house-roasted coffee and hot sandwiches, or Neel and Sawamura for coffee and a sit-down breakfast menu.
spots: A latte upstairs, watching the trains go by

moves.title: Explore the main “dori” shopping street
moves.text: Around the corner from Onibus is the neighbourhood's main shopping street, charming and full of shops and restaurants. Stop by Trasparente for freshly baked Japanese breads: shokupan, melon pan and curry pan.
spots: Shokupan, melon pan and curry pan

moves.title: Wander along the Meguro river and its shops
moves.text: Lots of local shops along the river: bamboo shoots for outdoor wear, Olgou and Kindal for used clothing, Coverchord and 1LDK for cool menswear, SML and Kinto for ceramics and tableware.

moves.title: Sit on a bench in the neighbourhood parks
moves.text: Meguro Sky Garden is a free little oasis built above a car park with incredible views of the city; look for the elevator at street level. Nearby, Sugekari Park and the connected Saigōyama Park have seasonal blooms and city views. On clear days you can see Mt Fuji from all three!
spots: A garden over the motorway; take the street-level elevator
Joined to Sugekari; Fuji on a clear day

moves.title: Walk into Daikanyama for a neighbourhood lunch
moves.text: Stand-outs for lunch: Tokyo Kenkyo for Japanese sandwiches including the popular egg sando, Omusubi Cafe for a classic Japanese lunch set, or Grigio, a cosy Italian-inspired restaurant.

moves.title: Flip through Japanese magazines at Tsutaya Books
moves.text: You can easily spend an hour flipping through the magazines at Tsutaya Books in the T-Site complex. Check out the Anjin bar upstairs for a midday cocktail or tea.
spots: Upstairs bar: a midday cocktail or tea

moves.title: Shop at local favourites
moves.text: Hollywood Ranch Market, Nanamica and their exclusive The North Face shop, Okura for indigo pieces, and iihoshi porcelain and Allegory Home Tools for ceramics and small home goods.
spots: Clothing, with an exclusive The North Face shop

moves.title: Visit a preserved Japanese home and garden
moves.text: Walk through Kyu Asakura House, a beautifully preserved Taisho-era residence with traditional wooden architecture, tatami rooms and a serene Japanese garden. Shoes come off at the entrance; put them in the storage area.
spots: Taisho-era house; shoes off at the door

moves.title: Make your way to Ebisu
moves.text: A business district by day, Ebisu transforms at night with a lively scene of izakayas and stylish cocktail bars. First, stroll along the river and swing by Inari Tea for an intimate tea experience, or Taiyaki Hiiragi for toasty red-bean-filled fish cakes with ice cream. If you need to store shopping bags, most stations have coin lockers by the hour.
spots: Taiyaki with red bean and ice cream

moves.title: A couple of shops you can't miss
moves.text: P.F.S Parts Center, a modern industrial hardware store; The Harvest Kitchen General Store for classic ceramics and tableware; Sukima for Japanese leather goods by Hender Scheme; Igamono for Japanese ceramics.

moves.title: Dinner in the neighbourhood
moves.text: For a lively dinner, Ebisu Yokocho: a nostalgic alley packed with izakayas serving grilled skewers, sashimi and cold beer. 67 Gyoza stands out for crispy cast-iron gyoza. For something quieter, Itasoba Kaoriya for traditional soba, CEDROS for California-style seafood, or Ta-im for Israeli staples.
spots: An alley of izakayas: skewers, sashimi, beer

moves.title: Sip at some local bars
moves.text: Winestand Waltz is a hidden, intimate wine bar; Bar Trench for craft cocktails; A10 for cocktails in a secret setting; Wine Bar Q or Spincoaster for a cosy bar playing records.

routes.tagline: Local bakeries, a park stroll, a Shinto shrine, the outskirts of Harajuku and observation decks
routes.reflect: What was the most unexpected joy or surprise you experienced today?

moves.title: Travel to Yoyogi-koen and explore Tomigaya
moves.text: Tomigaya is a laid-back pocket of Shibuya where Tokyo's creative crowd gathers: a short walk from the chaos of the crossing, but its own little world. For a quick coffee, Camelback Coffee or Little Nap. For a sit-down breakfast, Mukai for traditional donburi or Path for French-inspired dishes.

moves.title: Grab a pastry to go from the local bakeries
moves.text: Tomigaya has excellent bakeries: 365 Days for artisan breads, Levain for rustic sourdough, Nata de Cristiano for Portuguese custard tarts, and Harritts Donuts, a tucked-away neighbourhood favourite.

moves.title: Walk through Yoyogi Park
moves.text: Walk towards the Harajuku entrance and enjoy the pond, the rose garden and the seasonal blooms along the way.
spots: Enter by the Harajuku gate; pond and rose garden

moves.title: Explore Meiji Jingu
moves.text: Wander the beautiful Meiji Jingu Shrine area and look at the seasonal flowers in the Iris Field Garden (the irises peak in June; in winter it is the calm of the forest).

moves.title: Wander the outskirts of Harajuku
moves.text: Harajuku is more than Takeshita Street. Wander the area and stop by café-shop Think of Things, Labour & Wait for enamelware, Horaiya for coffee, and Beams Boy (women's) and Beams (men's) for popular Japanese clothing brands.

moves.title: Lunch in the neighbourhood
moves.text: Rojiura Curry Samurai for Japanese curry, Afuri for the famous yuzu ramen, Maisen for tonkatsu, Menchirashi for udon, Mr Farmer for wholesome salads, or Sahsya Kanetanaka for modern Japanese.

moves.title: Explore Cat Street and Takeshita Street
moves.text: Both are busy, but worth it. UNBY for camping goods, Cibone for modern homewares, Higuma Donuts or The Little Bakery, Tideway for handmade leather goods, Ragtag for secondhand clothing, 3Coins for ¥300 finds, a purikura photo booth, and Iyoshi Cola for Japanese natural soda. Then a 10-minute walk to Shibuya.

moves.title: Explore a depachika food hall
moves.text: The depachika, the department-store basement food hall, is in most big stores. The one in the Hikarie building (B3) is full of prepared savoury treats: onigiri, grilled skewers and bentos. On B2 are the traditional sweets, mochi and dorayaki. Great for snacks and souvenirs.
spots: B3 savoury and bentos; B2 sweets

moves.title: View Shibuya from the observation decks
moves.text: On the roof of Shibuya Scramble Square, Shibuya Sky is the highest point in Shibuya, a 360-degree open-air view of the skyline; reserve tickets in advance. If it is sold out, or for a free rooftop, the local secret is the roof of Parco, a trendy department store full of shops and food.

moves.title: Dinner in the neighbourhood
moves.text: D47 Shokudo, on the 8th floor of the Hikarie, has an epic view of the crossing in a calm setting; the menu is dishes from Japan's 47 prefectures. Also nearby: Kiwamiya for hamburger steak, Suage Soup Curry, Niigata Katsudon, Toritake, Matsue for sushi, Ryan for soba and Tsujita for tsukemen dipping ramen.
spots: 8th floor of the Hikarie; dishes from 47 prefectures

moves.title: Wander the crossing and around it
moves.text: Walking Shibuya crossing at night is iconic. Wander through Nonbei Yokocho and Miyashita Park, where you can sit on the rooftop with the locals. If you're up for more: Chatei Hatou, a hidden late-night retro café; INC, a low-key cocktail bar; or Jazz Bar Kohaku for live jazz.

routes.tagline: Iconic temples, traditional souvenirs, museums, the kitchen-supply street and classic Japanese meals
routes.reflect: What new cultural insight or tradition did you learn today?

moves.title: From Asakusa Station to the local cafés
moves.text: Known for its Scandinavian-Japanese aesthetic, Fuglen serves expertly brewed coffee and delicious waffles. Nearby, Cafe Tomorrow has more traditional breakfast sets and opens by 6:30.

moves.title: Explore the Sensō-ji grounds
moves.text: Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. The shops on Nakamise-dori open from 9am. Nearby specialty shops: Mokuhankan for traditional woodblock prints, Kanaya Brush, a traditional brush shop, Iyoshi Cola for natural soda, and Yonoya Comb Store, full of handmade combs.

moves.title: Wander to Sumida Park (3 min)
moves.text: Sumida Park gives you the Sumida River and an amazing view of the Tokyo Skytree. On the way, stop by the classic Fukuchan for yakisoba, or Kamakura Sweets and Kukurihime Cafe for traditional Japanese sweets.

moves.leg: 20 min train with one change, or a 14 min taxi: “Nezu-eki kudasai”
moves.title: Discover Nezu Shrine and its quiet streets
moves.text: Nezu Shrine is known for its red torii gates and tranquil garden. Nearby, Tokyo Bike rents beautifully designed bicycles by the hour or day. This area is best explored slowly, on foot or by bike: quiet residential streets, traditional tofu and rice shops, glimpses of everyday Tokyo. Check out Succession bakery across the street and Tasogaredō for handmade ceramics.

moves.title: A quiet neighbourhood walk to lunch
moves.text: Kayaba Coffee House is a local favourite known for its egg sandwich; sit upstairs in the traditional tatami room. Or Sampota Cafe Nombiriya for a cosy vintage-diner feel, or Sushi Noike for a traditional sushi lunch set.
spots: The egg sandwich; tatami room upstairs

moves.title: Explore the Yanaka Ginza shopping street
moves.text: Independent shops, snack bars and old-fashioned storefronts. Kanekichien for Japanese teas and ceramics, Yanaka Matsunoya for handmade baskets and everyday tools, Nito for retro café treats, and Beer Pub Ishii or Yanaka Beer Hall for local draft beer and shareable snacks.

moves.leg: From Nippori, one stop to Uguisudani (1 min), or a short walk
moves.title: From the end of Yanaka Ginza to Ueno Park
moves.text: Several large museums: the Tokyo National Museum, the Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum and the National Museum of Nature & Science. Stop for a traditional teahouse experience at Tohaku Chakan.
spots: At the end of Yanaka Ginza
National Museum of Nature and Science Ueno

moves.title: Explore the Ueno Park pond
moves.text: You could spend hours in the museums, but if you're ready for a slower pace, make your way to Shinobazu-no-Ike Pond to enjoy the water lilies and some people-watching by the lake.

moves.title: Travel to Kappabashi kitchen street
moves.text: Kappabashi is lined with shops for kitchenware and restaurant supplies: cookware, utensils, realistic food displays and custom lanterns. To narrow it down: KAMA-ASA for Japanese knives and their supply shop next door, FU WA RI for ceramics and wooden tableware, and Dengama for one-of-a-kind pieces.

moves.title: Dinner at a traditional restaurant
moves.text: Sometarō Okonomiyaki is a neighbourhood favourite for okonomiyaki, the savoury pancake of cabbage and batter with pork belly, seafood or cheese. Sushi Ken is another popular choice for traditional sushi. If you're up for a slightly longer walk, Kuramae Iseya is well worth it for beautifully prepared tempura.

routes.tagline: Independent coffee shops, a traditional garden, old Tokyo charm and classy neighbourhood gems
routes.reflect: Were there any new experiences from today that you'd like to bring into your daily life?

moves.title: Travel to Kiyosumi-Shirakawa
moves.text: A small coffee district and home to the beautifully preserved Kiyosumi Gardens. A neighbourhood made for slow mornings, scenic river strolls and a break from the city's pace.

moves.title: Enjoy the neighbourhood coffee shops
moves.text: Monz Cafe is a local favourite for sweet treats; Blue Bottle's warehouse location is one of the city's most beautiful; Koffee Mameya is sleek and modern; Iki Roastery serves great food along the river; Cafe Kokun has a nostalgic kissaten atmosphere.

moves.title: Explore the neighbourhood landmarks
moves.text: Kiyosumi Gardens is a must for seasonal blooms, along with the local museums: the Fukagawa Edo Museum and MOT, the Museum of Contemporary Art.

moves.title: Still up for more exploring?
moves.text: Rent a bike at Tokyo Bike and explore the area. Stop by the nearby Fujimaru Winery, enjoy traditional Japanese seafood at Kappou Miyako, unwind at the Tokiwa-Yu sento bathhouse, or browse ceramics at Canna, All and Potpurri.

moves.title: Travel to Ningyocho
moves.text: A neighbourhood full of old Tokyo charm: family-run traditional sweet shops, century-old restaurants and alleyways that feel like walking through a history book.

moves.title: A classic Japanese lunch
moves.text: Edoji is a quiet neighbourhood gem for grilled meats and seasonal vegetables. Shinodazushi specialises in inarizushi, tofu pockets filled with seasoned sushi rice, and traditional sushi bento boxes.

moves.title: Try the neighbourhood's traditional sweets
moves.text: Hatsune is a longtime favourite for classic Japanese desserts like parfaits and anmitsu. To take away: Itakuraya for their Seven Lucky Gods red-bean ningyoyaki, or Yanagiya for classic fish-shaped taiyaki.

moves.title: Japanese tea or a midday beer
moves.text: Morinoen specialises in hojicha roasted green tea; Xiaomei Tea House has Chinese teas and tea tools. For a midday beer, Number 6 nearby, or Craft Beer Market for Japanese beers.

moves.title: Make your way to Ginza
moves.text: Ginza is known for high-end shopping and retro charm, but at night it takes on a different energy: neon-lit streets, businesspeople buzzing between late-night bars, retro kissaten and Michelin-rated restaurants.

moves.title: Visit Ginza's specialty shops
moves.text: Among the familiar brands, a few you won't find anywhere else: Itoya, an upscale eight-floor stationery store; Takumi for handmade ceramics and Japanese home goods; Cibone Case on the 4th floor of Ginza Six, with modern decor; and Kyukyodo for quality Japanese paper and writing tools. The Muji Ginza flagship is worth visiting for its space alone, plus its specialty products, restaurant, bakery and hotel.
spots: The flagship, with a bakery and hotel

moves.title: Dinner in the neighbourhood
moves.text: Nemuro Hanamaru is a favourite for creative, seasonal conveyor-belt sushi; join the waitlist as early as possible with their remote QR system, as waits often reach two hours. Reserve Hachigou Ramen in advance for an elevated ramen; Oborodzuki for tsukemen; Yosuke Sato for udon; Torigin Honten for yakitori; Tamei-an for oyakodon and tempura in a classic setting.
spots: Conveyor-belt sushi; join the QR waitlist early

moves.title: Late-night coffee shops or bars
moves.text: Ginza is known for its late-night kissaten: Ginza West for classic desserts and tea, Tsubakiya Coffee or Ginza Ranzu for specialty coffee and sweets. For a drink, Mixology Salon for tea-based cocktails, or Bar Sherlock and Bar Chamucos for cocktails with homemade fruit syrups.

routes.tagline: Small cafés, the Shinjuku park, independent shops, cosy bars and unexpected creative cuisines
routes.reflect: Did you discover a spot today that you could see yourself returning to? Why?

moves.title: Travel to Shinjuku
moves.text: Shinjuku is best known for nightlife, but there's plenty for the day. Verve Coffee near the station opens at 7am with excellent coffee and waffles. Cafe Aaliya opens at 9am near the entrance to Shinjuku Gyoen, and Coffee Times is a classic kissaten known for buttered toast and its old-school smoking atmosphere.

moves.title: Explore Shinjuku Gyoen
moves.text: One of Tokyo's most beautiful parks. Seasonal gardens, small ponds, a greenhouse, spacious lawns, teahouses and small cafés. It's easy to spend a couple of hours here.

moves.title: Brunch in the neighbourhood
moves.text: Daian is a longtime favourite for its handmade soba and house-made soba tea.

moves.title: Specialty shops and department stores
moves.text: Sekaido, a well-known multi-storey art and stationery store; NEWoMan for contemporary fashion and design; Isetan, one of Tokyo's most iconic department stores; Beams for curated, design-forward gifts.
spots: Art and stationery over several floors

moves.leg: 33 min walk or 3 min train, Shinjuku to Hatagaya
moves.title: Start the walk through Hatagaya
moves.text: This begins a walk through Hatagaya, Nishihara and Yoyogi-Uehara: three overlooked neighbourhoods of independent shops, thoughtful cafés and local favourites, just beyond busy Shinjuku and Shibuya.

moves.title: The local take on global cuisines
moves.text: Despite its quiet residential feel, the neighbourhood is full of international flavours: Freeman Shokudo or Hoff for American-inspired comfort food, Dubois for French, Tortilla Club for Mexican tacos, Tsuta for creative ramen.

moves.title: Shop at independent local shops
moves.text: Rototo for socks made in Nara, Ella Records for a thoughtfully curated vinyl collection, and Bullpen and Roundabout for unique homewares and interior pieces.

moves.title: A coffee, wine or sweet break (or all three)
moves.text: Nadoya no Katte and Paddler's Coffee are neighbourhood favourites; Kasiki serves beautifully crafted ice cream; Haritts Donuts is known for baked donuts tucked away in a quiet alley. For something different, No. pairs coffee cocktails with a cosy bookstore, and Wineshop Flow has an excellent wine selection and bottle shop.
spots: Baked donuts in a quiet alley

moves.title: Tomigaya, Shibuya's quieter side
moves.text: Tomigaya is where many of Tokyo's creatives come to slow down. Its relaxed atmosphere, independent shops, neighbourhood restaurants and intimate bars make it a wonderful place to spend the evening.

moves.title: Neighbourhood specialty shops
moves.text: Lost & Found for Japanese tools and vintage-inspired glassware, Kihara for locally made pottery, Pivoine for French-inspired vintage clothing and home goods, and Shibuya Publishing & Books for artist pop-ups, curated books and unique stationery.

moves.title: The thriving dinner scene
moves.text: Kakan serves comforting Chinese dishes, Katsudon-ya Zuicho is known for juicy katsudon, ChowChow is cosy Italian, and Mimet pairs French-inspired cuisine with house-made desserts.

moves.title: End the evening at a neighbourhood bar
moves.text: Ahiru Store is a charming wine and snack bar; Cidernaut specialises in craft cider and seasonal dishes; Bellwood serves inventive cocktails in a speakeasy setting; Studio Mule is a wine and vinyl listening bar.

routes.tagline: Thrift shops, a relaxing pond, an underground café, the anime shopping centre and a neon-lit neighbourhood
routes.reflect: Were there any spots that inspired you creatively, through art, design or nature?

moves.title: From Shimokitazawa Station to a local café
moves.text: Shimokitazawa is known for its creative energy, vintage shops and independent cafés. Most stores open around 11am, but it's one of Tokyo's best neighbourhoods to wander slowly. Brooklyn Roasting Co. sits just outside the station; Sidewalk Coffee Roasters inside the Mustard Hotel opens at 7am with simple breakfast bagels; Ogawa Coffee Lab and Coffee Country Tokyo open by 9am nearby.
spots: In the Mustard Hotel; bagels from 7am
Sidewalk Coffee Roasters Mustard Hotel Shimokitazawa

moves.title: Breakfast or bakeries in the neighbourhood
moves.text: Universal Bakes Nicome, above Ogawa Coffee Lab, serves handmade pastries. RoJean offers comforting dishes like grilled cheese and soup, and Sandwich Club is open by 7am and specialises in a Japanese-style egg sando.

moves.title: Shop one-of-a-kind thrift stores
moves.text: Shimokitazawa is packed with vintage shops, so it's hard to know where to begin. Alaska, Top of the Hill and Furugiya Memento all have thoughtfully curated selections; Flamingo is a well-known Tokyo chain and Meadow by Flamingo offers a more mature curation.
spots: Top of the Hill vintage Shimokitazawa

moves.leg: 13 min on the express from Shimokitazawa to Kichijōji
moves.title: Begin at Inokashira Park
moves.text: Kichijōji is one of Tokyo's most beloved neighbourhoods. Begin at Inokashira Park, where walking paths wind around the pond past swan boats, a tranquil shrine and small coffee stands like Blue Sky Coffee.
spots: The pond and the swan boats
A coffee stand in the park

moves.title: Neighbourhood lunch gems
moves.text: Hikiniku to Come is known for juicy hamburger steak with rice; Kanekoya specialises in high-quality tempura; Iseya has been grilling yakitori since 1928; Tarekatsu is a favourite for crispy pork cutlets with seasonal vegetables, rice and miso soup.

moves.title: Local neighbourhood favourites
moves.text: PukuPuku for affordable vintage ceramics, 36 Sublo for thoughtfully curated stationery, Outbound and Sippo for Japanese homewares, clothing and accessories.

moves.title: A tea or coffee break
moves.text: Coffee Hall Kugutsusō is a hidden underground café that's been a neighbourhood favourite for decades; Chai Break is perfect for a takeaway chai before another walk around the pond.

moves.leg: 13 min on the local train from Kichijōji to Nakano
moves.title: Arrive in Nakano
moves.text: Nakano is a more down-to-earth side of Tokyo. As evening sets in, its cosy izakayas, neon-lit streets and nostalgic atmosphere make it a favourite among locals, yet it's often overlooked by visitors staying nearby in Shinjuku.

moves.title: Browse Nakano Broadway
moves.text: One of Tokyo's most iconic shopping complexes: anime collectibles, vintage toys, used electronics, watches, records, books and secondhand clothing. It feels uniquely Tokyo and is worth a little browse.

moves.title: Dinner and a neon-lit evening walk
moves.text: The streets around Nakano Broadway are packed with lively restaurants, tiny bars and lantern-lined alleys, best explored without much of a plan. Maguro Mart for exceptional tuna, Tototo for Japanese-style pizza, and Aonisai for a creative izakaya with excellent sake.

moves.title: Late-night cafés and bars
moves.text: Back inside Nakano Broadway, Coffee Zingaro is a colourful café made with Takashi Murakami, and Daily Chiko is famous for its towering soft-serve cones. For one last stop, Bright Brown is a cosy neighbourhood jazz and blues bar.

routes.tagline: A day along the Toyoko line: gentle strolls, local daily life, bookshops and high-quality Japanese food
routes.reflect: Is there someone you met today, a shopkeeper or a local, who left an impression on you?

moves.title: Travel to Jiyugaoka
moves.text: Spend the morning wandering Jiyūgaoka, a relaxed neighbourhood known for its tree-lined streets, independent shops and European-inspired atmosphere. The perfect place to slow down and see a quieter side of Tokyo.

moves.title: The neighbourhood's favourite cafés
moves.text: Onibus opens at 9am and has become a favourite among Tokyo's coffee lovers. Chanako Coffee Roastery and Alpha Beta Club are two more excellent morning options, each with thoughtfully roasted coffee and simple breakfast bites.

moves.title: Breakfast nearby
moves.text: Latte Graphic is a neighbourhood favourite for Australian-inspired breakfasts; Flipper's is known for its famously fluffy pancakes; for freshly baked pastries and sandwiches, Bread, Espresso, Jiyugaoka is well worth a stop.

moves.title: Browse the neighbourhood's specialty shops
moves.text: Today's Special is filled with tableware, kitchen tools, plants and gifts; Timeless Comfort specialises in ceramics and homewares; Popeye's Camera is a favourite for film photography supplies and camera gear. Although it opens later, Kosoan is a traditional teahouse that feels worlds away from central Tokyo.

moves.title: Arrive in Gakugei-dai
moves.text: A glimpse into everyday Tokyo. Fruit and vegetable stands spill onto the pavements, students make their way home from school, small independent businesses line the streets. It may seem unassuming at first, but it quietly rewards anyone willing to wander.

moves.title: Lunch in the neighbourhood
moves.text: Stand Banh Mi is a longtime favourite for modern Vietnamese sandwiches; Midorie serves seasonal deli-style plates built around fresh vegetables.

moves.title: Browse the independent shops
moves.text: Book & Sons is a curated bookstore for art and design, with a rotating gallery upstairs. Around the corner, Sunny Boy Books has a wonderful selection of secondhand books, Tokyo Recycle imption is filled with vintage homewares, and Yuyujin showcases beautifully curated pottery.

moves.title: A coffee or sweet break
moves.text: Matterhorn is a longtime neighbourhood favourite for cakes, cookies and seasonal desserts, takeaway or seated. Higuma Doughnuts serves warm made-to-order doughnuts, while Woodberry Coffee and WR. are excellent cafés tucked beneath the train tracks.

moves.leg: 30 min walk through Yutenji, or 3 min train
moves.title: Travel to Nakameguro
moves.text: Walking toward Nakameguro you pass through Yutenji, another quiet residential neighbourhood full of independent shops and small eateries. A calm place for slow wandering.
spots: A quiet neighbourhood on the way

moves.title: Dinner with the locals
moves.text: Nakameguro is filled with excellent restaurants. Jazzy Beats serves modern, high-quality ramen; Kakura is known for its house-made Japanese curry; Seirinkan has a reputation for some of Tokyo's best pizza; Source specialises in okonomiyaki; Kushiwakamaru is a lively yakitori restaurant with a classic izakaya atmosphere straight out of a Japanese film. Join the waitlist early on their clipboard, as it fills up quickly.

moves.title: Browse vintage and specialty shops
moves.text: Jantiques is one of Tokyo's best vintage shops; Cul De Sac specialises in Japanese hinoki wood products; Migratory curates tableware and local clothing brands; Fabrik crafts leather goods on site; Okashi Machioka has one of the neighbourhood's best selections of Japanese candy and packaged snacks.
spots: One of Tokyo's best vintage shops

moves.title: End the evening with a drink or dessert
moves.text: Oasis is a favourite for craft beer; Epulor for craft cocktails and snacks in a vinyl bar; Rokusho is a hidden tequila bar tucked into a residential street; Huit for a late-night dessert and tea in a charming setting along the Meguro river.

routes.tagline: An elegant day of neighbourhood gems, artisan bakeries, contemporary art and a memorable evening in Roppongi
routes.reflect: What did you notice when you slowed down? What sight, sound or smell stood out most today?

moves.title: From Omotesando Station to a local café
moves.text: Aoyama is where refined architecture meets quiet luxury: polished yet calm. Start the day at Koffee Mameya for beautifully prepared coffee in a minimalist setting, or Chavaty for handmade scones and specialty tea drinks.

moves.title: Brunch options nearby
moves.text: i2 Cafe is known for Dutch baby pancakes and specialty toasts; Little Pool Coffee for Japanese omurice; Sahsya Kanetanaka for beautifully presented Japanese set meals.

moves.title: Flip through Japanese books and magazines
moves.text: Aoyama Book Center is a longtime favourite tucked behind the United Nations University, with an inspiring selection of Japanese books and magazines. On a weekend, the Aoyama Farmer's Market just outside is well worth a stop for local snacks, produce and handmade goods.

moves.title: One of Tokyo's best bakeries
moves.text: Stop by Amam Dacotan or Breadworks Omotesando for fresh pastries before continuing your walk.

moves.title: Get lost in the Spiral building
moves.text: Spiral Market is a multi-storey cultural space with a rotating gallery, café, shop and a collection of independent shops. While you're here, stop by Call Cafe or book a tea tasting at Sakurai Tea Experience, known for beautifully prepared teas and tea-based cocktails.
spots: A cultural space with a gallery
On the 5th floor of the Spiral

moves.title: An introduction to ikebana
moves.text: The Ohara School of Ikebana is one of Japan's most respected schools of flower arranging and offers introductory classes for visitors. Sign up in advance.
spots: An introductory class; sign up ahead

moves.title: Lunch in the neighbourhood
moves.text: Yanmo is a cosy basement restaurant known for grilled fish set meals; A to Z Cafe serves quality lunch sets in a relaxed setting; Cicada is a longtime favourite for Mediterranean cuisine; tucked away off the main street, Hachi is known for its wagyu dishes.
spots: Grilled fish sets, in a basement

moves.title: Explore the nearby museums
moves.text: The Nezu Museum is celebrated for its striking architecture, its collection of Japanese and East Asian art and one of Tokyo's most peaceful gardens. Nearby, the Taro Okamoto Memorial Museum preserves the artist's former home and studio, filled with vibrant sculptures and mid-century furniture.
spots: Asian art and a beautiful garden

moves.title: Visit the independent shops
moves.text: Tucked away from the main path, Pejite is a favourite for one-of-a-kind ceramics; Encounter Madu and Utsuwa Omusubu specialise in tableware, teaware and home goods; Tsutaya for ikebana tools, vases and tea ceremony pieces.

moves.leg: Walk over through the Aoyama Cemetery
moves.title: Make your way to Roppongi
moves.text: Roppongi is known for nightlife, but it has a polished, contemporary side. Walk over from Aoyama through the Aoyama Cemetery, surprisingly peaceful with its tree-lined paths, and stop at the National Art Center, 21_21 Design Sight or Tokyo Midtown for contemporary art and shops.
spots: Peaceful tree-lined paths on the way

moves.title: A traditional dinner setting
moves.text: Jomon is a lively neighbourhood favourite for grilled skewers; Butagumi specialises in exceptional tonkatsu in a traditional setting; Nishiazabu Taku has an intimate sushi counter on a quiet street, perfect for a special evening (reservations recommended).

moves.title: End the evening with music or dessert
moves.text: Soul Bar George's is an intimate listening bar with a jukebox of Motown and oldies. For live jazz, Blue Note is one of the city's most iconic venues; reserve tickets in advance. If you'd rather end over tea and dessert, Ginza West is a retro late-night café with tea and homemade cakes.

routes.tagline: Charming bakeries and cafés, unique shops, traditional curry and a bridge with neon-lit river views
routes.reflect: Which moment felt the most uniquely “Tokyo”, one you can't find in any other big city?

moves.title: Travel to Kuramae
moves.text: One of Tokyo's best neighbourhoods for discovering local makers. Small bakeries, artisan workshops, independent cafés and thoughtfully designed shops give the area a creative yet unpretentious atmosphere.

moves.title: Early-morning cafés and breakfast spots
moves.text: Lonich offers a unique coffee omakase; Daily's Muffin serves savoury and sweet muffins; En specialises in Japanese breakfast plates and thick-cut toast; Pelican is a longtime favourite for charcoal-grilled shokupan sandwiches and toasts.

moves.title: Browse a few independent shops
moves.text: Kakimori is known for beautifully crafted stationery, custom inks and personalised notebooks. Mizukiya Baba Shoten specialises in handmade baskets; Kimura Shop is a charming stop for traditional kites and toys; REN showcases handcrafted leather goods.

moves.title: A takeaway treat from a local bakery
moves.text: Yogashi Lemon Pie is a charming tiny pie shop; Shinonome Seipansho is an excellent stop for freshly baked pastries. Before leaving, pick up beautifully packaged cookies from Kashiya Shinonome and tea from Nakamura Tea Life.

moves.leg: 14 min train with one change, Kuramae to Jimbocho
moves.title: Travel to Jimbocho
moves.text: One of Tokyo's great book neighbourhoods, where secondhand bookstores, retro kissaten and a slower pace give the area a timeless charm.

moves.title: Lunch nearby
moves.text: Jimbocho is known for its long-standing Japanese curry restaurants. Curry Bondy is a neighbourhood institution; Rice Curry Manten and Ethiopia are two more local favourites.

moves.title: Browse the bookstores and shops
moves.text: Bumpodo for art and stationery, Magnif for vintage magazines, and Komiyama for art and photo books.

moves.title: Recharge at a classic kissaten
moves.text: Jimbocho's classic cafés are reason enough to visit. Dill Coffee Parlor has an old-school coffeehouse atmosphere; Koseto for coffee and cakes with a whimsical feel; Jazz BIGBOY for the vinyl; Milonga Nueva for a hidden, cosy hideaway.

moves.leg: Walk, or a short train ride
moves.title: Make your way to Akihabara
moves.text: Best known for electronics and anime culture, Akihabara takes on a completely different atmosphere after dark, with glowing neon signs and memorable stops beyond the main attractions.

moves.title: Explore the Mansei bridge area
moves.text: The Manseibashi bridge is well worth a stop, especially after dark, when neon reflects across the river and passing trains make one of Tokyo's most cinematic views. Stop by Hitachino Brewery for a drink on the riverside terrace before continuing.
spots: Neon on the river, trains overhead

moves.title: Browse Akihabara's unique shops
moves.text: Maach Ecute Kanda Manseibashi is a former train station now full of shops, restaurants and a museum. Tokyo Radio Department Store fascinates electronics enthusiasts; Super Potato is packed with vintage video games and collectibles; Akihabara Gachapon Hall is the place to try Japan's capsule-toy machines.

moves.title: A casual dinner
moves.text: Ginzo is tucked beneath the train tracks, serving fresh sushi to the rumble of trains overhead. Tempura Hisago is a longtime favourite for classic tempura; Tonkatsu Marugo is known for exceptional tonkatsu.

routes.tagline: The iconic seafood market, quiet garden moments, classic midday meals and traditional shops
routes.reflect: How did today's walk connect you with the city? Did the pace feel right? What would you change next time?

moves.title: Start at Shimbashi, in the Hamarikyu Gardens
moves.text: Before Tsukiji, spend the morning wandering Hamarikyu Gardens, where seasonal flowers and walking paths make a peaceful escape from the city. Visit the Nakajima Tea House for traditional matcha and sweets.
spots: Matcha and sweets on the pond

moves.title: Stroll through the Tsukiji seafood market
moves.text: Tsukiji is still one of Tokyo's most exciting food destinations. It gets busy, but the generations-old vendors, sizzling food stalls and morning energy make it well worth experiencing at least once.

moves.title: Step away from the crowds
moves.text: After the main market, slow things down with breakfast at Tsumugi, where traditional Japanese morning sets are served in a peaceful setting (reservations recommended). Turret Coffee is a neighbourhood favourite for espresso drinks; Atelier Matcha specialises in beautifully prepared matcha.
spots: Japanese breakfast sets in the temple; reserve

moves.leg: Tsukiji to Takebashi, 20 min with one change
moves.title: Quiet moments surrounded by nature
moves.text: The Imperial Palace area is a change of pace from the rest of the city: wide walking paths, landscaped gardens and plenty of open space, plus the National Museum of Modern Art and Chidorigafuchi Park.
spots: National Museum of Modern Art Tokyo

moves.title: Arrive in Kagurazaka
moves.text: Tucked into a quieter side of Shinjuku-ku, Kagurazaka is a charming mix of old Tokyo and subtle European influence, with the river nearby. Narrow backstreets, small bistros and hidden shops: an absolute hidden gem.

moves.title: Settle in for a classic midday meal
moves.text: Once home to geisha houses and traditional restaurants, Kagurazaka still carries a quiet refinement. Ishiusubiki Teuchi Kyōrakutei for handmade soba, Kurobatei for udon, Wacha for traditional tea and light snacks, or Brasserie Gus for a French-inspired lunch in a charming setting.

moves.title: Ten minutes' walk to a traditional garden
moves.text: Since you're nearby, Koishikawa Korakuen Garden is a short walk away and keeps the traditional atmosphere going. Admire the seasonal plants, or stop for lunch in the garden at Kantoku-tei.

moves.title: A break at the local favourite cafés
moves.text: Akha Ama Coffee or Elm Green are great for a coffee and a handmade slice of cake; Arbor Coffee is known for seasonal drinks and Japanese purin. Stop by Weekenders Coffee for coffee and books.

moves.title: Browse the traditional neighbourhood shops
moves.text: Rakuzan is a wonderful place to bring home high-quality Japanese teas; Akomeya and Koharuan specialise in pantry goods, kitchenware and everyday essentials. Hidden in the residential side, うつわや 釉 (Utsuwaya Yu) and Jokogumo showcase handcrafted ceramics, and the Cat Post Office is a quirky stop for cat lovers.
spots: うつわや 釉 神楽坂

moves.title: Dinner in the neighbourhood
moves.text: Ryūhō is a longtime neighbourhood favourite for Chinese cuisine, Stefano for comforting Italian, and Sakura is well known for its excellent tonkatsu.

moves.title: End the night with a drink or dessert
moves.text: Kagurazaka Saryō is perfect for traditional Japanese desserts; Aux Merveilleux specialises in delicate French pastries. To toast the end of the trip, K.West and Bar Ahiru-Sha are both excellent vinyl bars, and Mushin offers wine and light bites in an intimate setting.

rest.title: Rest day
rest.tagline: Self-care ideas for the day nobody wants to walk
rest.note: Some need a reservation; check the website first.

spots.name: Olive Spa Ebisu
spots.text: A classic for a reason: the go-to for a luxurious reset. Private rooms, deep relaxation treatments and their signature heated stone therapy make it feel like an escape from Tokyo's non-stop energy.

spots.name: Shibuya Saunas
spots.text: A hidden oasis in the middle of Shibuya, blending sleek modern design with traditional sauna culture. Dry heat or a cold plunge: perfect for winding down after a long day of exploring.

spots.name: Waho-an Nature
spots.text: Omotenashi, Japan's signature hospitality, done properly: holistic treatments blending shiatsu, acupuncture and herbal therapies to help you realign and recharge.

spots.name: Head Spa Kuu
spots.text: A full sensory experience using gentle water therapy and deep scalp treatments. Perfect for relieving stress, and you leave with extra-glossy hair.

spots.name: Assort Tokyo
spots.text: Known for expert cuts and effortless styles, this international salon is a trusted go-to for travellers looking for a refresh with a Tokyo touch.

spots.name: Thermae-Yu
spots.text: Natural hot-spring water in the middle of Shinjuku. Book an evening.

spots.name: Bunka Yokusen
spots.text: There are countless smaller neighbourhood sento (communal hot baths). This one has modern updates, cool merch and jazz on the speakers, and is popular with the younger crowd.
